title: squalify must profile Parquet files through DuckDB
lead:
Adds the `parquet` family.
- It reads file metadata, the schema, row groups and key/value metadata keys through DuckDB.NET.Data.Full 1.5.5.
- It streams every row, in one thread and in order, into the shared field accumulators, so Parquet fields have the same profile shape as text.
- It adds the Parquet fingerprint contribution and the `parquetColumns` hint.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** expanding nested columns (only count, nulls and `sourceType`); hive directories (directory input is not in v1).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Goal: the v1 formats.

Owner decision: DuckDB.NET.Data.Full 1.5.5, the same pin as DataBall. DataBall checked that `DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM read_parquet(path)` returns exactly the top-level columns, and that `PAR1` sits at both ends of the file (`DataBall/src/DataBall/FileProbe.cs:69-75` and `:86-104`).

The column lists for the `parquet_*` functions come from the current, unversioned duckdb.org docs and must be checked against 1.5.5.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/squalify/squalify.csproj`: adds `DuckDB.NET.Data.Full` 1.5.5.
- `src/squalify/Parquet/ParquetProfiler.cs`: scores 1.0 when the `parquet` magic matches at both ends. It uses an in-memory connection set up with `SET threads=1; SET preserve_insertion_order=true;`.
  - `parquet_file_metadata`: `num_rows`, `num_row_groups`, `format_version` and `created_by`. `created_by` names the writer software, so it is always included.
  - `parquet_schema`: top-level columns, plus the physical, logical and converted types and the repetition.
  - `parquet_metadata`, aggregated in `row_group_id` order:
    - `dialect.rowGroups {count, rows {min, max}, compression[], encodings[]}`, with the sets sorted;
    - per column, `statisticsPresent`.
  - `parquet_kv_metadata`: `kvKeys` always; values only with `--include-values`.
  - Rows: `SELECT * FROM read_parquet(?)`, read through a `DbDataReader`, with typed values passed to the accumulators.
- Type mapping:
  - BOOLEAN → bool.
  - INT8 to INT64 and UINT8 to UINT32 → int. UINT64 → int, or float when a value exceeds Int64.
  - FLOAT and DOUBLE → float.
  - DECIMAL → float, with `sourceType` `DECIMAL(p,s)`.
  - DATE → date; TIMESTAMP (any precision or time zone) → datetime; TIME → time.
  - VARCHAR → string.
  - BLOB → string, with `sourceType` and length statistics only.
  - STRUCT, LIST and MAP → `type: null`, with `sourceType`, count and nulls only.
- `src/squalify/Parquet/ParquetFingerprint.cs`: `layout` adds the column names in order with their repetition; `typed` adds the physical and logical types.
- Hints: `parquetColumns`.
- Fixtures:
  - generated in the test setup through DuckDB `COPY (…) TO '<tmp>/x.parquet' (FORMAT PARQUET, ROW_GROUP_SIZE n)`;
  - `parquet/sweep.parquet`, committed as a golden input, produced by `tests/squalify.Tests/fixtures/parquet/make-sweep.sql`, which is documented so it can be regenerated.
- `docs/design.md` "Parquet"; `docs/descriptor.md` `format.dialect` for Parquet.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Parquet_SchemaAndTypes_Mapped` (theory over each DuckDB type in the mapping).
2. `Parquet_FieldStats_MatchCsvOfSameData`: profiling the sweep as CSV and as Parquet gives equal numeric statistics and types.
3. `Parquet_RowGroups_Aggregated`.
4. `Parquet_KvValues_OnlyWithFlag`, plus a canary theory row.
5. `Parquet_Nested_CountsOnly`.
6. `Parquet_TruncatedFile_DescribedAsBinaryWithIssue`.
7. A golden for `parquet/sweep.parquet`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Check the column lists of `parquet_file_metadata`, `parquet_schema`, `parquet_metadata` and `parquet_kv_metadata` against DuckDB 1.5.5, and record them in a slicer note.
2. Write the tests.
3. Implement.
4. Mutation check: drop `threads=1`, and confirm the golden stays stable or a test catches the ordering change. If it stays stable, note why.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `dotnet build squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet test squalify.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet format squalify.sln --verify-no-changes`
- CI is green on all three OSes. DuckDB ships native binaries per platform.
- If this slice changed architecture (the pipeline, an interface, a descriptor section or a determinism rule), `docs/how-it-works.md` and its diagrams are updated and `./scripts/render-docs.sh` has been re-run. The architect confirms there is no drift.
- `slicer check`

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/sq-08` on branch `sq-08`. No agent commits. After the gate returns `VERDICT: PASS`, the orchestrator commits `sq-08: Parquet profiler` when the owner approves.
